title: Fix atomicity in token refresh path to prevent cross-organization session leakage
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported authentication and authorization anomalies starting 2026-02-28. Symptoms included: API keys/refresh tokens unexpectedly granting access to resources belonging to a different org, and long-lived sessions surviving KMS rotations in Private installs. Severity escalated when two enterprise customers reported data exposure to other org-scoped metadata.

What happened (short):
A race condition in the token refresh codepath allowed an old session-to-org mapping to persist in Redis/metadata cache while the new token was issued and returned to the client. This mismatch combined with a degraded cache-write path (multi-region async replication) and a fallback validation path for legacy token signatures in the Private validator produced scenarios where a valid token authenticated but resolved to the wrong org_id.

Components affected:
- Hosted API refresh endpoint (refresh orchestration service)
- Dedicated control-plane session-store replication between availability zones
- Private on-prem token validator fallback logic and KMS key rotation handling

Immediate customer impact:
- 3 medium/enterprise customers reported at least 1 cross-org metadata read (no confirmed data exfiltration beyond metadata; we are auditing).
- Several customers experienced failed re-auths after KMS rotation in Private installs, leading to degraded UX and manual rekeying requests.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Create two orgs A and B with API keys and active sessions.
2) Trigger near-simultaneous refresh requests for a session in org A from two different regions (simulates client retry + load balancer).
3) Observe interleaving: refresh service issues new token, writes org mapping to Redis write-behind queue; concurrent stale cache read returns old org mapping for auth lookup.
4) In Private installs with KMS rotation enabled, rotate keys; legacy validator fallback accepted signed token but resolved org lookup via stale mapping.

Root cause analysis (technical):
- Token refresh handler performed non-atomic sequence: issue_new_token -> write_org_mapping_async -> return_token. The async mapping write used eventual-consistency replication (write-behind queue). Under concurrency, a race allowed auth queries to see the old mapping while the client presented the new token.
- Redis keys for session->org were short-lived and subject to eviction and replication lag in Dedicated multi-AZ configurations.
- Private validator had a compatibility fallback for legacy signatures that bypassed an authoritative KMS-backed validation path when the local KMS plugin returned a transient error. That fallback path consulted the local cache which was stale after rotation.

Mitigations applied (emergency):
- 2026-02-29 03:12 UTC: Disabled async write-behind on refresh path for Hosted; flipped to synchronous write-through with a CAS check while we investigate.
- 2026-02-29 04:25 UTC: Issued scoped API key rotations for affected orgs and forced session revocation for sessions with suspicious org mismatch patterns.
- 2026-03-01 01:00 UTC: Deployed temporary Private hotfix: KMS plugin now fails closed (no legacy-fallback) on transient KMS errors and surfaces error to ops to avoid accepting tokens that bypass authoritative validation.
- Notified impacted customers with initial incident notice and offered hands-on remediation and key rotation assistance.

Short-term (next 72h) plan:
- Stabilize Hosted by leaving synchronous write-through enabled while we harden testing.
- Run an audit job to surface sessions with session->org last-updated timestamps older than token issuance and flag for forced re-auth.
- For Dedicated, increase Redis replication consistency (quorum-writes) for session keys and add telemetry to detect replication lag beyond 200ms.

Long-term fixes planned (postmortem):
- Ensure the refresh path is atomic: implement single atomic operation at the datastore layer (Redis LUA transaction or central metadata service transaction) that both issues token and binds session->org mapping. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3157)
- Add end-to-end concurrency tests in the auth integration harness that simulate cross-region refresh races and KMS rotations.
- Remove legacy validator fallback in Private; instead implement retry with exponential backoff and alerting, and require a quorum of KMS replicas for positive validation.
- Add a 'session-authority-version' stamp to tokens and mapping entries so that mismatch is detectable and leads to forced re-auth instead of silent acceptance.
- Create an onboarding checklist for Private customers that validates KMS rotation behavior as part of install and upgrade.

Rollout and verification plan:
- Merge PR-3157 into canary edge cluster (runtime-1.30-canary) and run 48-hour canary traffic with synthetic refresh load that reproduces the race.
- If canary is stable, roll to Hosted primary (regions eu-west-1, us-east-1) in staged waves over 24 hours.
- For Dedicated customers, schedule maintenance windows to increase Redis write durability and apply agent updates.
- For Private customers, provide a scripted upgrade and KMS configuration validation runbook; offer direct migration support for customers who experienced the issue.

Customers & comms:
- Customers impacted: Acme Analytics (priority incident), Nimbus Payments, and two SMB customers (names redacted).
- Communication sent: Initial incident notification, technical follow-up with remediation options, and final postmortem planned after rollout is complete.
- Compensation: expedited key rotation + 25% credit for impacted billing month if data access confirmed.

Monitoring & detection updates:
- New alert: session-org-consistency-alert triggers when token_signature_time > session_org_last_updated_by > 30s for > 5 unique sessions in 1m window.
- Dashboard: auth-consistency (link: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/auth-consistency) added panels for regional replication lag, refresh latency, and KMS error rates.

Open action items (owner):
- Ravi Patel: finish PR-3157, add LUA transaction, implement new unit+integration tests (estimate 8).
- Lina Gomez: lead Dedicated Redis durability work and schedule customer maintenance (estimate 5).
- Simon Reed: Private validator cleanup, remove fallback, and implement KMS quorum checks (estimate 8).
- Maya Thompson: customer comms and compensation approvals, coordinate SOC + legal involvement (estimate 3).

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- No cross-org auth anomalies observed in canary for 48h under synthetic load.
- Audit job shows zero sessions with token issuance newer than session->org mapping for all Hosted traffic.
- Dedicated nodes report replication lag <= 50ms and no alerts for 24h post-change.
- Private installs with KMS rotation run the upgrade and pass the validation runbook.

Post-incident retrospective items:
- Update runbooks to include emergency disable/enable toggles for async write-behind and KMS fallback layers.
- Add explicit section in customer onboarding for KMS rotation verification.
- Quarterly chaos test covering token refresh races across regions.
